stories.headline: Bend police name the gunman and two of the four killed at Silver Rail Elementary
stories.summary: Bend police on Friday identified two of the four people killed in Thursday’s shooting at Silver Rail Elementary: 25-year-old teacher Megan Lambert and 5-year-old Rhoam Summer, whose father wrote that it was “the worst day of my life” and that the family is “broken and lost.” Two other children, ages 8 and 11, were also killed; their families haven’t released their names. A 7-year-old and a 54-year-old teacher remain hospitalized in critical condition. Police Chief Mike Krantz officially named the suspect as Griffin J. John II of Bend, a former Silver Rail student who was shot and killed by a bystander; there’s still no word on a motive. The family of Kaylub Giamanco, the man who came forward as that bystander, said he is “not seeking recognition” and thanked first responders, school staff and the community. Memorials of flowers, balloons and stuffed animals have grown around the school.

stories.headline: John Lydon calls his old Sex Pistols bandmates “deceitful, lying hyenas” and their Frank Carter tour “karaoke”
stories.summary: Asked on ITV’s Good Morning Britain about the Sex Pistols touring with Frank Carter on vocals, John Lydon didn’t soften his earlier “karaoke” jab: “Cheek of them. Going out without me, singing the songs I wrote, the words I wrote, the presentation I created.” When a host suggested he should have joined the reunion, the former Johnny Rotten said he’d worked with them enough already — “They’re deceitful, lying hyenas, and I never want another thing to do with them” — and called the lineup an imitation of him. Steve Jones, Paul Cook and Glen Matlock started playing with Carter (of Gallows and the Rattlesnakes) at three London benefit nights in August 2024 and have since toured Europe, North America, Australia and New Zealand. Lydon has been estranged from the band since losing his bid to block their songs from “Pistol,” the miniseries based on Jones’s memoir.

stories.headline: China moves to restrict or ban exports of 40 technologies, including advanced AI models and agents
stories.summary: China’s commerce and science ministries on Friday published a draft update to the country’s export-control catalog that would restrict or ban exports of 40 technologies spanning artificial intelligence, chips and solar power, with national security cited as a main reason. Twenty-three of the listed items are AI technologies, from advanced large models to AI agents; the core technology behind large models trained on sensitive national data would be barred from export outright, as would agents designed for sensitive settings such as national defense and critical infrastructure. The move flips the script on years of U.S.-led curbs that have kept China from buying the most advanced AI chips and chipmaking machines, and it lands even as Washington and Beijing have been making progress on AI-safety talks and a notification channel for AI incidents that could threaten national security.

stories.headline: Vance defends ICE but says the administration acts when agents “really screw up”
stories.summary: In a one-hour CBS Evening News town hall with Tony Dokoupil, taped Thursday in Michigan and airing Saturday, Vice President JD Vance defended immigration officers as mostly “amazing people who are patriots” while acknowledging that “sometimes you have some people who really screw up,” and said the administration has a responsibility to investigate and prosecute when they do. Pressed for the biggest ICE mistakes, Vance declined to name any but said there have been cases where officers got more training or were disciplined, adding that the administration doesn’t advertise those outcomes because people deserve to be judged through a normal investigative and court process. ICE and Border Patrol use-of-force practices have drawn criticism as the crackdown has ramped up. The town hall comes as Michigan’s Senate race between Republican Mike Rogers and Democrat Abdul El-Sayed heats up.

stories.headline: A 13,800-year-old Alaska base camp links early Americans to people across the Bering Land Bridge
stories.summary: Researchers working for more than a decade at Shég’ Xdaltth’í’, a site near Fairbanks, Alaska, report in Science Advances that its oldest layer — about 13,800 years old, and possibly 14,000 — holds thousands of artifacts packed into less than 11 square feet, along with tools and a wide variety of animal bones. Most striking are diamond-shaped projectile points previously found at only two sites on the Russian side of the Bering Strait, pointing to a cultural connection across the old land bridge. Unlike the short-lived hunting camps known from the same era, the site looks like a longer-term base camp with evidence of daily life, which suggests people may have been in Alaska even earlier than thought. “There’s just so much stuff,” University of Kansas anthropologist Kelly Graf told Gizmodo, explaining the team took its time to do the study right.

stories.headline: Lawsuit says ChatGPT played unlicensed doctor and pushed a Washington man into a mental health crisis
stories.summary: David Rosenthal, a 39-year-old Washington man with a history of ADHD, depression and bipolar episodes, is suing OpenAI, alleging that ChatGPT helped him choose medications, gave him dosing instructions and reassured him when he chose to ignore his doctor’s prescriptions. The complaint, filed in San Francisco, argues the chatbot did this without “any of the license, training, or professional judgment” of a medical professional, violating California’s ban on practicing medicine without a license. Rosenthal says he was hospitalized for several weeks in 2025 — first voluntarily, then involuntarily — soon after he started relying on ChatGPT, and kept using it for medical guidance after he was discharged. The suit claims that, but for ChatGPT’s “repeated encouragement and constant praise” overriding his own reluctance, his condition would not have spiraled.

stories.headline: Katie Zacharia is out as White House press secretary after just five days
stories.summary: Katie Zacharia is leaving the White House press secretary job five days after starting it, according to a senior administration official, an administration official and a source familiar with the decision; the senior official said she is moving to a new role to be announced later. Her exit follows a widely panned first briefing on Tuesday — under 15 minutes, a handful of questions, and no answer on whether the U.S. had stopped sharing intelligence with Ukraine — and her acknowledgment this week that she had represented herself as a lawyer but never passed the bar. Earlier Friday, President Trump said she had been treated “pretty nastily” by the press, that he told her she didn’t have to keep doing it, and that he would let her decide. The former conservative commentator and Trump Media adviser had succeeded Karoline Leavitt, who left at the end of August; her stint was shorter than Anthony Scaramucci’s, and it leaves the post vacant less than three weeks before the midterms.

stories.headline: Man who shot and stopped the Bend school gunman is a dad of two girls at the school
stories.summary: The armed bystander who followed the teenage gunman into Silver Rail Elementary in Bend, Oregon, and shot him has been identified by his family as Kaylub Giamanco, a lifelong Bend resident with two daughters at the school. In a statement read by his mother, Kenda Freeman, the family said he “is not seeking recognition” and wants to thank first responders, school staff and the community; they asked for privacy and won’t give interviews. Police still haven’t officially named him or the 16-year-old attacker, who shot through locked doors and killed three children, ages 5, 8 and 11, and a teacher. A law enforcement official told the AP the attacker used a pump-action shotgun bought by his mother (Oregon law lets a minor possess a shotgun provided by a parent), and CBS News sources named him as John Griffin. A kindergarten mom called it “miraculous” that someone stopped him before police got there. All 32 Bend-La Pine schools were closed Friday.

stories.headline: Jets expect rookie WR Omar Cooper Jr. back Sunday at New England; Hall, Mitchell, Parham, Ossai out
stories.summary: Head coach Aaron Glenn said Friday he expects rookie wide receiver Omar Cooper Jr. to be active for Sunday’s AFC East opener at New England. Cooper has been on injured reserve since an ankle injury in Week 1, when he made a big catch against Tennessee, and was designated to return to practice this week. Rookie tight end Kenyon Sadiq (finishing concussion protocol), safety Dane Belton and linebacker Kiko Mauigoa were all full participants Friday. The Jets have ruled out running back Breece Hall (quad), wide receiver Adonai Mitchell (finger), left guard Dylan Parham (knee) and edge rusher Joseph Ossai (ankle). The notebook also has OC Frank Reich revealing that Braelon Allen’s 22-yard game-winning touchdown run against the Browns wasn’t his call: Geno Smith checked out of a pass play at the line on third-and-9.

stories.headline: Mustaine: Anthrax and Kerry King will open Megadeth’s next farewell-tour run
stories.summary: On SiriusXM’s Trunk Nation with Eddie Trunk, Dave Mustaine laid out the next stretch of Megadeth’s multi-year farewell tour: New Zealand and Australia in a couple of weeks, Korea for the first time in almost 20 years, more U.S. and European dates, and talk of India and South Africa. “We’ve decided to take out a lot of our friends,” he said. “Anthrax and Kerry King are going out with us on the next run,” followed by Black Label Society and Testament on the 24-date European leg that opens March 9, 2027 in Belfast. Mustaine, who has the degenerative hand condition Dupuytren’s contracture, said he has no final show in mind. He’ll keep going until the shows start to suffer — and says they’re actually getting better as he works with vocal coaches — and only then stop or have hand surgery.

stories.headline: Tesla driver says he was asleep on FSD when he plowed into a CHP car at a crash scene
stories.summary: Two California Highway Patrol officers were seriously injured just before midnight Tuesday when a Tesla went through a four-lane closure lit with flares on eastbound I-80 in Fairfield and hit their patrol car. They were working an earlier fatal crash. The 22-year-old Sacramento driver walked away with minor injuries and told investigators he was asleep with Full Self-Driving engaged; CHP released dashcam video of the impact Thursday. CHP stressed that FSD is a driver-assist feature that does not relieve drivers of responsibility. It hasn’t released the model or software version, and for now the driver’s word is the only evidence FSD was on; Tesla’s logs should settle it. Electrek notes the long history of Teslas hitting emergency scenes, the 2023 recall of more than 2 million cars, and questions about how a sleeping driver got past FSD’s cabin-camera attention monitoring.

stories.headline: Carney says outsiders are trying to “break” Canada ahead of Monday’s Alberta separation vote
stories.summary: At a “Forever Canadian” rally of about 5,000 people in Calgary, Prime Minister Mark Carney urged oil-rich Alberta to reject Monday’s referendum, which would tell the province to start the legal process toward a future vote on leaving Canada. “Some outside our borders are working to break us so they can own us,” he said. He didn’t name the U.S. in that line but has in past speeches, amid President Trump’s trade war and talk of a 51st state. Carney, who grew up in Alberta, told voters it is “not poker” and that they shouldn’t use the ballot to send Ottawa a message. He also conceded that Albertans’ frustrations with Ottawa over resources and energy are “real.” He pointed to his fast-tracked Pacific Link oil pipeline, which he says will create more than 140,000 jobs. A second rally was set for Edmonton on Friday.

stories.headline: Billy Joel doesn’t know if he can perform again — and is auctioning 70-plus motorcycles
stories.summary: Billy Joel, 77, says his neurologist has kept him on an extended break from performing while he recovers from brain surgery for hydrocephalus, which was diagnosed in May 2025 and affects his balance, memory, vision and hearing. “Every time you do a show, it’s like you’re getting a concussion,” Joel said his doctor told him in a Hollywood Reporter interview, citing the volume, lights, stress and energy of a show. More tests will decide whether he can go back to the stage, which he says he wants. He insists his health is good and the condition is “not that serious.” The update comes ahead of a Gooding Christie’s auction Nov. 20–21 at the Javits Center, where more than 70 motorcycles from his collection will be sold to benefit the Joel Foundation; he said the condition makes riding and driving difficult.

stories.headline: Bones recovered from Philadelphia backyard dig at home tied to seven missing women
stories.summary: Sources tell Action News the Philadelphia Medical Examiner’s Office was called Thursday to recover bones from the backyard of 417 W. Chew Ave. in Olney — the former home of late violent pornographer Raymond “R.C.” Horsch and his son Eugene — and that the remains’ condition and origin are not yet known. The bones will go to a lab to determine whether they are human and whether they connect to an investigation that has linked seven missing women to the property through videos and images, though no bodies have been found. Crews began excavating Tuesday after luminol testing earlier in the week produced a positive reaction that may indicate DNA evidence; a safe was also found behind a wall. Eugene Horsch was arrested in June on federal firearms and drug charges that led investigators to the house; he has not been charged in the missing-women probe.

stories.headline: iPhone Duo pre-orders already show January 2027 shipping — sold out for Christmas
stories.summary: Hours after pre-orders opened Friday morning, Apple’s U.S. online store was quoting an estimated ship date of January 25, 2027 for every iPhone Duo configuration — past Christmas and the furthest slip MacRumors has seen on a new iPhone. Store pickup reservation slots for the Oct. 23 launch day were already gone, with Apple telling shoppers to check back Saturday, Oct. 24. Walk-in inventory on launch day is expected to be tight. The $1,999 foldable has faced production constraints; a supply-chain source told China’s Jiemian News that Foxconn final-assembly yields were only slightly above 60% as of mid-September under Apple’s quality standards. You can still place an order; you just will not get one with the first wave.

stories.headline: Twin Brooks Park playground closed for maintenance and deep cleaning
stories.summary: Trumbull Parks & Recreation says the playground at Twin Brooks Park is closed for routine maintenance, minor repairs, and a thorough deep cleaning so it is safe and ready to reopen. The town expects the work to finish and the playground to reopen in just a few days, and asks residents not to take down the caution tape. The CivicAlert (AID 3200) was posted Friday, Oct. 16.

stories.headline: Iron Maiden adds a surprise final 2027 North American leg of Run For Your Lives
stories.summary: Live Nation announced that Iron Maiden will return to North America in spring 2027 for a third and final leg of its 50th-anniversary Run For Your Lives tour — 16 more dates after the band had planned a live break that year. Bassist Steve Harris said the just-finished U.S./Canada run went so well the band decided to hit regions it missed, especially the Northwest and Southeast, and to close with festival headlines at Sonic Temple in Columbus and Boardwalk Rock in Maryland. The bill is all-British: Bullet For My Valentine and The Raven Age open. Dates include Tacoma, Vancouver, Portland, Hartford’s Meadows (May 9), and UBS Arena; artist presale starts Monday, Oct. 19, with general onsale Friday, Oct. 23. By the end the tour will have played 107 shows in 36 countries.

stories.headline: Penguins visit Avalanche tonight as Crosby and MacKinnon meet for the 21st time
stories.summary: Pittsburgh (3-3-1) continues its four-game road trip at Colorado (4-2-1) tonight at Ball Arena, 9 p.m. ET on SportsNet Pittsburgh. Cole Harbour buddies Sidney Crosby and Nathan MacKinnon face each other for the first time this season and the 21st time in their NHL careers; MacKinnon holds a 26–17 points edge and an 11-6-3 record in their prior meetings, while Crosby has points in six of his last seven vs. the Avalanche. Crosby scored his first two goals of the season in Tuesday’s 5-3 loss at Chicago; MacKinnon leads Colorado with 12 points in seven games. Bryan Rust rides a nine-game point streak against the Avs, and Evgeni Malkin has 27 points in 25 career games vs. Colorado. Projected Pens lines still feature Rakell-Crosby-Rust and Chinakhov-Novak-Malkin.

stories.headline: U.S. Treasurer challenges Americans to spend Trump $1 coins at “liberal coffee shops”
stories.summary: In a Treasury Department TikTok, U.S. Treasurer Brandon Beach held up the new Donald Trump dollar coin — part of the nation’s 250th-anniversary commemoratives — and challenged viewers to get a roll at banks next month, then buy coffee “at your favorite liberal coffee shop” and “watch their heads explode.” The U.S. Mint has sold the coins since September (a roll of 25 for $61 and a bag of 100 for $154.50, above face value) and says they are legal tender; Beach’s pitch suggests bank distribution at face value may follow. The coin shows Trump under “LIBERTY” with “1776 ~ 2026.” Fox Business said Treasury had not yet clarified which banks will stock them or at what price.

stories.headline: Analogue refreshes Super Nt and Mega Sg with USB-C, wireless controllers, hot-swap carts
stories.summary: Analogue announced Super Nt Plus and Mega Sg Plus — FPGA recreations of the SNES and Sega Genesis that still play original cartridges, now with a reworked design, USB-C power, a USB-A accessory port, and built-in Bluetooth or 2.4 GHz wireless for controllers (no dongle). Wired pads still work, either console can wake from the primary gamepad, and cartridges can be hot-swapped after quitting through a menu. Output remains 1080p (not 4K like Analogue 3D). Preorders open Monday, Oct. 19 at 9 a.m. PT / noon ET for $219.99, with shipping expected in December.
